title: Power Pages: self-service site ownership transfer in the admin centre
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents an API for the SAS logging setting that the controls table reports as undocumented. The auditing setup instructions also omit Microsoft's required domain allow-list prerequisite, without which most SAS functionality will not work.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Reading Power Platform activity logs in Purview requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs.
claims.quote: To view Power Platform activity logs in Microsoft Purview, users need to be assigned either the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Power Pages logging prerequisites require configured auditing for the production environments being monitored.
claims.quote: Configure and turn on auditing for the Power Platform production environments you want to monitor

claims.claim: The option to turn on audit logging is visible only when the minimum Office licensing requirements are met.
claims.quote: The option to turn on audit logging is only visible when the minimum Office licensing requirements are met.

claims.claim: A Power Platform system admin or customizer configures auditing and the SAS logging setting.
claims.quote: A Power Platform system admin or customizer needs to configure auditing in the Power Platform admin center and then turn on the Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting
claims.fix: Keep the cited overview's requirement but note that https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/security/data-storage#turn-on-purview-audit-logging instead specifies a tenant admin for the logging toggle; the overview's step-by-step toggle procedure specifies signing in as a system admin.

claims.claim: SAS logging uses Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Privacy and Security > Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings > Enable SAS Logging in Purview.
claims.quote:
Select Manage in the navigation pane.
Select Environments in the Manage pane.
Expand the Product list and select Privacy and Security.
In the Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings section, toggle the Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting to On.

claims.claim: No API for the environment's Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting is documented.
claims.quote:
"LoggingEnabledForIpBasedStorageAccessSignature" = $true
-Method Patch -Uri "https://api.powerplatform.com/environmentmanagement/environments/$environmentId/settings/?api-version=2022-03-01-preview"
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].api=null with a power-platform-api entry using PATCH https://api.powerplatform.com/environmentmanagement/environments/{environmentId}/settings/?api-version=2022-03-01-preview and body {"LoggingEnabledForIpBasedStorageAccessSignature":true}; cite this tutorial and label its API preview. The current reference also documents PATCH .../settings?api-version=2024-10-01 at https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/power-platform/environmentmanagement/environment-management-settings/update-environment-management-settings. Do not change EnableIpBasedStorageAccessSignatureRule merely to enable logging.

claims.claim: The SAS logging setup instructions tell admins to enable the setting without the domain allow-list prerequisite.
claims.quote: Before you activate the Shared Access Signature (SAS) feature, add the https://*.api.powerplatformusercontent.com domain to the allow list. If you don't, most SAS functionalities won't work.
claims.fix: Prepend to the SAS logging checklist instruction and add to controls[2].note: 'Before enabling SAS logging, allow access to https://*.api.powerplatformusercontent.com; Microsoft warns that most SAS functionality will not work without this prerequisite.' The same requirement explicitly covers either SAS feature at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/security/data-storage#storage-shared-access-signature-sas-ip-restriction.

Search for and select Microsoft Entra ID.

Select the website app from the list of available applications.
Under Manage, select Owners.
Select Add owners.

claims.claim: The website app is the separate Entra application registration named Portals-<website name>.
claims.quote:
A website app owner is a user who owns the website application registration in the Azure portal.
This application is called Portals-<<website name>>.

claims.quote:

POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications/{application-object-id}/owners/$ref

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages site licensing is capacity based, using authenticated users and anonymous users per website per month.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.claim: The cited licensing FAQs say nothing about ownership transfers.
claims.quote: Searched: transfer|ownership in the fetched full text of https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-flow-licensing-faq; no matches. Also searched Power Pages ownership transfer licensing and read the returned licensing excerpts.

claims.claim: The admin roles page says website ownership remains with the creator and cannot be transferred or changed.
claims.quote: The website owner is the user who created the Power Pages website. While you can update website management roles, ownership remains with the creator and can't be transferred or changed.

claims.claim: The transfer page and admin roles page describe different ownership concepts.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer site ownership and ownership transfer eligibility; opened learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/transfer-ownership and admin/admin-roles. Both discuss site ownership; neither states that their conflicting ownership descriptions are different concepts.
claims.fix: Replace 'The two Learn pages describe different ownership concepts and do not explain the difference' with 'The two Learn pages appear to conflict and do not explain how the transfer relates to creator ownership.' Do not assert a documented distinction between ownership concepts.
